clauses.reason: The title and enacting words of EO 10346 state the order's subject, preparation by Federal agencies of civil defense emergency plans, and the authority under which the President acted: the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950 and his position as President and Commander in Chief; they operate only through the three numbered sections that follow, so they ended with the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 10346: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (4), "Executive Order No. 10346 of April 17, 1952.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 1 of EO 10346 directs each Federal department and agency, in consultation with the Federal Civil Defense Administration, to prepare plans for providing its personnel, materials, facilities and services under section 302 of the Federal Civil Defense Act during a civil-defense emergency, taking into account the essential military requirements of the Department of Defense. It was a continuing planning duty. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 10346: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (4), "Executive Order No. 10346 of April 17, 1952.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision. Later events: EO 10773 (Secs. 3 and 4(a)(3)) amended references to the Federal Civil Defense Administration in EO 10346, and EO 10782 amended the name EO 10773 uses for the successor office; they changed references and did not end this provision.

Section 2 of EO 10346 directs each department and agency to prepare, in addition to the section 1 plans, plans for maintaining the continuity of its essential functions at the seat of Government and elsewhere during a civil-defense emergency, using personnel, materials and facilities exclusive of those needed for the section 1 plans and consulting the Federal Civil Defense Administration on civil-defense aspects. It gives the National Security Resources Board authority to establish standards and policies for uniform continuity planning, and makes the portion of a continuity plan involving functions at the seat of Government effective on approval by the President and the portion involving functions performed elsewhere effective on approval by the head of the department or agency. It was a continuing duty. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 10346: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (4), "Executive Order No. 10346 of April 17, 1952.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision. Later events: EO 10438 transferred the functions vested in the National Security Resources Board under EO 10346 to the Director of Defense Mobilization and amended the order accordingly; EO 10773 (Secs. 3, 4(a)(3) and 4(b)(4)) amended references to the Federal Civil Defense Administration and to the Office of Defense Mobilization; EO 10782 amended the name EO 10773 uses for the successor office; and EO 11051 (Sec. 601(3)) amended references to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization in the penultimate sentence of Section 2 only. They are amendments and do not end the provision.

Section 3 of EO 10346 directs the Federal Civil Defense Administrator to assist the departments and agencies by indicating the types of personnel, materials, facilities and services considered useful for civil-defense purposes in time of emergency, to arrange for the use of those not required for maintaining the continuity of essential functions, and to coordinate the arrangements with national, State and local civil-defense plans. It was a continuing duty. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 10346: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (4), "Executive Order No. 10346 of April 17, 1952.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision. Later events: EO 10773 (Secs. 3 and 4(a)(3)) amended references to the Federal Civil Defense Administrator in EO 10346, and EO 10782 amended the name EO 10773 uses for the successor office; they changed references and did not end this provision. EO 10529 cites Section 3 of this order and is not a change to it.

research_rationale:
EO 10346 (1952-04-17; Preparation by Federal Agencies of Civil Defense Emergency Plans) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (17 FR 3477, Federal Register of 1952-04-19), whose file also contains neighbouring material; the order was delimited by its heading and the Harry S. Truman signature line. The dossier's machine segmentation, which cuts sections into lettered fragments and repeats some, was replaced by 4 scopes: one for the enacting words and one for each numbered section. Its own terms contain no end date, expiry or termination condition. It ended on 1969-10-28 by express revocation in EO 11490, Sec. 3015, item (4), cited from the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 255823; page record checked: heading, date and text hash agree with the held text) and read for corroboration in the Federal Register print of 34 FR 17567 onward (OCR text), which lists the same order. Later instruments naming it: EO 10438 (functions of the National Security Resources Board under this order transferred to the Director of Defense Mobilization, 1953-03-13), EO 10773 (reference changes, effective on signing 1958-07-01 as recited by EO 10782 in its text), EO 10782 (amends EO 10773, effective as of 1958-08-26) and EO 11051 (Sec. 601(3), 1962-09-27) are recorded as later events on the scopes they touch; EO 10529 only cites Section 3 of this order. None ends it. I did not hold the part of EO 10773 printed on the Federal Register page after the held first page, so only its Secs. 3 and 4 as printed there are relied on. The selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog) are coverage statements read before use; they are leads, not independent review.

savings.reason: Item (4) of Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 revokes EO 10346. In the held American Presidency Project transcription, Sec. 3014 reads: "Except as provided by Section 3015, nothing in this order shall be deemed to derogate from any now existing assignment of functions to any department or agency or officer thereof made by statute, Executive order, or Presidential directives, including Memoranda." Because Sec. 3014 begins with that exception, it does not preserve the revoked order. The end source span cited for this claim runs from "SECTION 501. Functions." through Sec. 3015, that is Parts 5 through 30 of EO 11490. I read Sec. 3014 and Sec. 3015; I did not read the other Parts to decide whether any of them carries this order's commands forward, so no transfer or accrual is claimed and the state is none_after_bounded_search.
